title: date_diff_in_days absolute difference
means: Returns the absolute value of the difference in days between two dates or DateTime. The reader projects the function result as delta; the Endpoint must execute the documented function, not ignore its arguments.

title: date_diff_in_seconds absolute difference
means: Returns the absolute value of the difference in seconds between two DateTime. The reader projects the function result as delta; the Endpoint must execute the documented function, not ignore its arguments.

title: date_diff_in_minutes absolute difference
means: Same behavior as date_diff_in_seconds, but returns the difference in minutes. The reader projects the function result as delta; the Endpoint must execute the documented function, not ignore its arguments.

title: date_diff_in_hours absolute difference
means: Same behavior as date_diff_in_seconds, but returns the difference in hours. The reader projects the function result as delta; the Endpoint must execute the documented function, not ignore its arguments.

title: date_diff explicit date format
means: The page's exact microsecond-format example: date_diff_in_seconds('2022-12-19T18:42:23.521Z', '2022-12-19T18:42:23.531Z', date_format='%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fz'). The absolute difference is below one second. The reader projects the function result as delta; the Endpoint must execute the documented function, not ignore its arguments.

title: date_diff backup date format
means: backup_date_format: (optional) the format of the dates if the first format does not match. Use it when your default input format is a DateTime (2022-12-19 18:42:22) but you receive a date instead (2022-12-19). The reader projects the function result as delta; the Endpoint must execute the documented function, not ignore its arguments.

title: date_diff none_if_error permits alternate logic
means: none_if_error: whether to return None if the dates do not match the provided formats. Use it to provide alternate logic in case any date is specified in a different format. The reader’s alternative is -1 when the result is None.

title: Pipe creation refuses wrong SQL

title: replace_condition filters incoming rows
quote: The replace condition filters the new data that's appended, meaning it excludes rows not matching the condition.
means: Published conditional-replace rule, with the guide's profession partition and profession=Jedi condition. The reader-supplied CSV includes a matching and a nonmatching row to assert the stated exclusion; its exact fixture bytes are not claimed as the guide's jedi.csv. The readback asserts the matching new row, the excluded new row, and the existing row in another profession partition.
